# software-design-philosophy

Curated by Skill Harbor: John Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design, distilled into a working skill for code reviews, architecture discussions, and API design. It covers the three symptoms of complexity (change amplification, cognitive load, unknown unknowns), strategic versus tactical programming, deep versus shallow modules, information hiding and leakage, pulling complexity downward, defining errors out of existence, designing everything twice, and the philosophy of comments and naming, with a red-flags quick reference (shallow module, temporal decomposition, pass-through method, vague names, comment repeats code, and nine more) to run through during reviews. By @hotopla5976, listed here with credit to its creator. Discovered via github.com/topics/ai-skills. Honest caveats: this is a study guide distilled from a published book, use it as a working reference and read the book for the full depth; it is plain text, there is nothing to install beyond reading it. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
